alerts: Critical: Active Knock Retard detected during High Load.

chat_history.content: what are the issues cause by this tune?

[Engine State]
The primary operational state during the logged period was Wide Open Throttle (WOT), accounting for 83.2% of the log time, with an average RPM of 4660.0 and an average load of 168.6 kPa.

[Observation]
A peak knock retard value of 2.49° was recorded during high-load operation. This value exceeds the normal threshold of 2° and falls into the warning category. This knock event occurred despite optimal Intake Air Temperatures (peak 17.2°C) and Air-Fuel Ratios (average 11.55 AFR during WOT, with no observed leaning at higher RPM/load).

[Severity]
Warning

[Explanation]
The presence of knock retard, even at a peak of 2.49°, indicates that the engine control unit (ECU) detected pre-ignition or detonation and initiated timing reduction to protect the engine. This is particularly notable given the consistently rich WOT AFRs (11.31-11.54) and exceptionally low intake air temperatures, which typically mitigate knock risk. The occurrence of knock under these otherwise favorable conditions suggests that the base ignition timing calibration may be overly aggressive for the current engine configuration or fuel octane.

[Possible Causes]
- Aggressive ignition timing calibration for the specific engine hardware or fuel octane.
- Inconsistent fuel quality or lower-than-specified octane rating.
- Minor mechanical factors contributing to localized hot spots or combustion instability.

[Confidence]
High
